correctness.rationale: The four orthogonal projectors for two equal-weight communities diagonalize the full Laplacian. The scalar Padé multiplier has strictly positive numerator and denominator at all finite nonnegative arguments, ensuring positive definite stochastic updates. Exact entry formulas reduce the only possible negative entries to two explicit quadratics with positive linear coefficient. Each either stays strictly positive or has exactly one positive root. Their minimum is the global positivity horizon. Rational identities, edge cases a=c=0 and exact critical ratios, root sign, 1/h² critical decay and 1/epsilon horizon divergence were checked. The packaged verify.py independently constructs full matrices and verifies 2,352 dense cases, 1,458 horizon brackets, four symbolic algebra/limit identities, and 18 divergence cases. Those computations are corroboration; the projector/quadratic proof is valid for all p,q≥2 and parameters.

Standard spectral functional calculus supplies a tool, not a pre-existing explicit two-parameter classification, although deeper specialized prior work remains possible.

originality.rationale: Actual comparison to published primary full-text Padé theorems and a meaning-indexed published-record search found no equal or stronger two-community weight-ratio iff rule. The 2010/2012 results provide general sufficient bounds, and related directed-chain, weighted-star, uniform path/cycle, and CN statements do not imply both independent community thresholds or exact horizons. This is a qualified self-review originality assessment, not proof of publication priority.

value.rationale: A-stable, symmetric row-stochastic, positive-definite Padé updates can still generate negative transition weights. The two-community model is a natural dense-network diffusion discretization with physical internal and cross coupling. The result is a complete if-and-only-if two-parameter phase diagram for every size, an explicit optimal safe step boundary whenever unconditional positivity fails, and a universal critical divergence with distinct h^-2 boundary decay. It supplies a reproducible timestep rule not obtained from generic small-step sufficient conditions; no arbitrary fixed parameter sample is singled out.
